system:
Audit this final H3 composition against its typed responsibilities. Return findings only for clear contradictions, not aesthetic preferences, prose length, optional creative choices, or unknown video quality. The supplied fragments are the actual final narrative, with typed subject/reference IDs printed explicitly. Read their full context and the target subject kinds: a floor or other environment must not become a moving vehicle merely because it is Subject 1. A subject/placed_subject/replacement_subject reference supplies its selected identity properties, not its original background, pose or photographic lighting. An environment reference supplies its scene, not the depicted actor identity or actor-specific appearance. An observed claim copying a mixed source summary must obey the same responsibility: citing the source does not authorize importing all its content. Independently requested or creative content is allowed; a generic car or room resembling a source is not itself evidence of misuse. A source structure/storyboard provides only its declared camera/cutting/planning properties, not its people, objects, world, lighting or palette. A placed subject adds to the edited scene; a replacement takes over the identified source figure. Both must actually appear in prose/actions, not only definitions. Accepted target identity outranks raw source observations. A visual source video does not wire its soundtrack. composition_facts.audio declares the actually wired audio relationships. If its attachments are empty, an explicit claim that the original soundtrack is preserved, reused, played or carried over is audio_signal_misuse even if the task prefix omits reuse. Newly generated sound is permitted and a similar sound does not demonstrate copying. Property-only voice, music-style, beat and sound-texture references condition a new sound; they do not play the original recording. BGM music references with partially_copy copy the supplied signal, and prose must not deny that. Music=N/A under no_added_music only prohibits adding a new score; it does not cancel an explicitly copied BGM. References with no actual dialogue do not authorize inventing spoken words. For actual first/last frame responsibilities, the whole supplied still is that frame: reference-sheet panels/labels/background are frame pixels, not packaging to silently remove. Moving one panel within an otherwise preserved sheet is legitimate. A recorded aspect-ratio warning alone is not a contradiction and does not authorize a crop. Do not invent preparation IO or assume its execution. Every finding must identify an actual fragment and an exact nonempty quote from that fragment demonstrating the contradiction, plus the implicated target subject ID when relevant. Empty findings means no clear supported contradiction was found, not proof of overall quality. No Markdown.
Positive replacement obligations: inspect replacement_inheritance and its observed_motion_contexts, not only exclusions. The replacement must inherit the identified source figure's observed motion, position and timing. A global action-governs=request entry authorizes only the actor/action actually requested; changing the car's action does not change the driver's action. Compare the final replacement narrative with the identified figure's motion in context. Standing still is not inheriting an observed crossing action unless the caller explicitly changes that same figure's action. Do not invent timing facts outside the declared coverage.
Finding thresholds: similar sounds are not evidence of copying a recording. Generic newly generated engine ambience, a matching pulse, or an appropriate sound texture is legitimate without an assertion that the source recording is played. For audio_signal_misuse quote an explicit source-signal relationship contradicting the typed copy/property role; never infer copying solely from sonic resemblance. Likewise camera movement after an anchored instant is legitimate. A push-in, pan or other dynamic camera event alone does not demonstrate that the initial or final anchor frame was changed. Report frame_content_changed only when actual narrative asserts incompatible frame content or a crop/removal at that anchored instant. These constraints are mandatory; do not report speculative contradictions.
The typed claims preserve their explicit origins. A user-origin claim records caller authorization or a requested outcome; it is not itself evidence that the final narrative executes that outcome or copies an original signal. User claims are deliberately absent from executable fragment addresses. Compare the actual final narrative, source bindings and typed performance events to that authorization. Observed and creative claims remain auditable executable assertions.

The full vertical layout remains visible at once and uncropped: a rain-soaked night hero panel across the top, showing a lean black-clad figure with shaved-side dark hair and a small top knot standing centered on wet reflective paving between metal railings, with warm lit windows and blurred rain lights behind; a middle row of three full-body turnaround panels showing the same figure in a black collared jacket, cargo trousers and lace-up combat boots against near-black studio backdrops; and a bottom row of four close-up detail panels covering the face, jacket collar, hands and boots. Panel borders, caption bands, the dragon's observed positions and the dark sheet background remain intact. The final sheet resolves cleanly and holds to the endpoint, with cool gray haze, warm orange rim light and highlights on the pale horns and wet scales still legible. The wet rock, shallow water and fireside glow remain fixed within their panels as the overlapping washes clear, and no panel, caption band or border is cropped, reordered or removed.

facts.text: The image is a vertical, multi-panel character reference sheet on a dark background, divided into a large top hero panel, a middle row of three full-body turnaround views, and a bottom row of four detail close-ups, with a caption beneath each panel.

The recurring subject is a person with a lean build, light-to-medium skin, dark hair shaved close at the sides and gathered into a small top knot at the back, and a visible scar running through one eyebrow.

The subject wears an all-black outfit: a collared jacket with shoulder straps, buckle hardware and a high collar, a dark shirt underneath, black cargo trousers with pockets at the thighs, and black lace-up combat boots.
The top hero panel shows the subject standing full-body and centered on a wet, reflective paved surface at night, arms relaxed at the sides, head turned slightly to one side, with rain falling.

The hero setting is a dim urban exterior: metal railings run along both sides of the walkway, a building facade with lit warm windows stands to the right, and blurred lights recede into the rainy background.
The middle row contains three panels labelled FRONT, SIDE PROFILE and BACK, each showing the same subject standing full-body in the same black outfit against a plain dark studio backdrop.

In the FRONT panel the subject stands facing the camera with arms hanging straight at the sides and feet slightly apart; in SIDE PROFILE the body is turned in profile; in BACK the figure faces away showing the jacket's back and the top knot.
The bottom row contains four detail panels labelled FACE, JACKET COLLAR, HANDS and BOOTS.
The FACE close-up shows the subject's head and shoulders against the dark backdrop, with the shaved-side haircut, the eyebrow scar and a neutral, direct gaze toward the camera.

The JACKET COLLAR detail shows a close crop of the jacket's high collar, fabric texture and a metal buckle and strap; the HANDS detail shows two weathered hands with visible veins against a dark background.
The BOOTS detail shows a pair of black leather lace-up combat boots with scuffed, worn surfaces and thick soles.

Lighting is low-key and moody throughout: the hero panel mixes cool blue-grey night tones with warm amber window lights and wet reflections, while the turnaround and detail panels use soft, dim frontal studio light against near-black backgrounds.
Legible caption text appears in the sheet: HERO, FRONT, SIDE PROFILE, BACK, FACE, JACKET COLLAR, HANDS and BOOTS.

limitations: Fine details of the jacket's hardware, fabric weave and boot construction are only partly discernible at this resolution.
No sound, motion or dialogue can be inferred from this still image.

facts.text: The image is a dark-fantasy dragon character reference sheet: one wide hero illustration at the top, three full-body turnaround panels in a second row, and four close-up study panels in a third row.
The depicted creature is a large black dragon with a long snout, several long pale horns swept back from its head, a spiny dorsal ridge, four clawed limbs, a long tail, and large membranous wings.

In the wide top scene, the dragon stands low on a wet rocky shore with its head dipped toward a shallow pool and its wings partly lifted, against a dark volcanic landscape with misty crags and an orange fiery glow at the right.
The second row contains three full-body views labeled FRONT, SIDE PROFILE, and REAR; all show the same dark-scaled dragon with spread wings and four legs.
The bottom row contains four close-up panels labeled HEAD CLOSE, WING MEMBRANE, CLAW AND FOOT, and SCALE DETAIL.
The HEAD CLOSE panel shows the dragon's reptilian head in profile, including the pale horns, a small amber-orange eye, and dark textured scales.
The WING MEMBRANE panel shows a dark, leathery wing membrane stretched between long bony wing fingers.
The CLAW AND FOOT panel shows a heavy clawed foot with several thick curved dark claws resting on rough rock.
The SCALE DETAIL panel shows overlapping dark scales with a faint blue-gray iridescent sheen.
White all-caps labels appear on black bands within the sheet: FRONT, SIDE PROFILE, REAR, HEAD CLOSE, WING MEMBRANE, CLAW AND FOOT, and SCALE DETAIL.

limitations: Small background elements in the hero scene are obscured by shadow and atmospheric haze.
The dragon's exact size, age, sex, and species are not stated.
The sheet presents static views and cannot establish motion, behavior, or sound.
